title: Drop tower-log from the default features
body:
- [x] I have looked for existing issues (including closed) about this

## Feature Request
tower-log was added in #218 because tower 0.4 enabled its log feature (which turns on tracing/log) by default. axum disabled tower's defaults and exposed log as its own feature, and made it default since that's what tower did.





### Motivation
tower 0.5 doesn't have any default features anymore, so log is opt-in there now. axum still enables it by default though, so every app using axum's defaults gets tracing/log turned on for every crate in its dependency graph, even though tower itself stopped doing that. Because features are unified, the only way to opt out is default-features = false and listing all the other defaults again. #659 had the same concern for axum-extra.
<!--

-->

### Proposal
I'd suggest removing tower-log from default in the next breaking release and keeping the feature so people can still opt in. Happy to send a PR.

title: Support for the HTTP QUERY Method
body:
- [x] I have looked for existing issues (including closed) about this

## Feature Request

### Motivation

Recently the [RFC 10008](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc10008/) standardized the HTTP QUERY method, which is also registered at the [IANA HTTP Method Registry](https://www.iana.org/assignments/http-methods/http-methods.xml#methods). In short, this new method is a mix of GET and POST method: it's safe and idempotent like GET but also has a body like POST.

### Proposal

The QUERY HTTP method should be added to `axum::routing::MethodFilter` as well as the `axum::routing::method_routing` module and any other place where HTTP methods might be handled.

### Alternatives

There is no known real alternative other than using either GET or POST method, which is not ideal.

title: Support custom SSE event
Ensure generated multipart boundaries do not occur in part data
body:
## Summary

`MultipartForm` documents that a multipart boundary should not occur in the data, but the implementation generates one boundary and serializes all parts without checking for collisions.

## Affected code

- `axum-extra/src/response/multiple.rs:36` generates the boundary.
- `axum-extra/src/response/multiple.rs:52` serializes the parts.
- `axum-extra/src/response/multiple.rs:212` documents the boundary invariant.

## Why this matters

The chance of a random collision is tiny, but this module already has all parts in memory. Enforcing the invariant would make the implementation match the documented behavior at low cost.

## Proposed fix

Add a private `generate_boundary_for_parts(&[Part])` helper that retries if the candidate boundary appears in any part body or relevant serialized metadata.

Use a bounded retry loop and return an internal server error only if repeated attempts fail.

## Acceptance criteria

- Boundary generation checks candidate boundaries against all parts.
- A test forces a collision and verifies a different boundary is chosen.
- Normal multipart responses are unchanged.

title: Allow customizing the executor used by `axum::serve`
body:
- [x] I have looked for existing issues (including closed) about this

## Feature Request

### Motivation

`axum::serve` hardcodes `TokioExecutor` for spawning connection tasks and hyper's internal HTTP/2 tasks. This is the one thing that can't be customized from the outside, you have to reimplement the entire serve loop (~150 lines) just to swap the executor.

We hit this in [dial9-tokio-telemetry](https://github.com/dial9-rs/dial9-tokio-telemetry) where all spawned tasks need to be wrapped to capture scheduling delays and wake events. Our workaround was a full [reimplementation of `axum::serve`](https://github.com/dial9-rs/dial9-tokio-telemetry/blob/main/examples/metrics-service/src/axum_traced.rs).

### Proposal

Add a `Serve::with_executor()` builder method. Default executor stays `TokioExecutor`, so it's fully backward compatible.

```rust
axum::serve(listener, router)
    .with_executor(my_executor)
    .await;
```

### Alternatives

- Use hyper/hyper-util directly: works, but you lose all of axum's serve conveniences (graceful shutdown, accept loop, error handling). This is what the docs currently suggest.
- Reimplement `axum::serve`: ~150 lines of boilerplate that tracks axum internals and breaks across versions.

title: Remove unwrap() in Router::fallback_endpoint by using a take-once service wrapper
body:
-[yes] I have looked for existing issues (including closed) about this
Summary

Router::fallback_endpoint currently relies on an Option + unwrap() pattern inside service_fn to ensure the fallback route is only consumed once. This assumes the service is never called more than once; if that invariant is violated, it panics in the request path.


Location

router/mod.rs — Router::fallback_endpoint (see existing TODO: “get rid of the unwraps”).


Problem (conceptual)

The fallback service is wrapped in Option and consumed via service.take().unwrap() inside a FnMut.
If the service is ever called more than once (due to misuse, future refactors, or edge cases), this results in a panic instead of safe handling.


Expected

The fallback route is consumed once, and any unexpected reuse is handled safely (no panic in prod).

Actual

A second call triggers unwrap() and panics.



Proposed approach

Replace the Option + unwrap() pattern with a small internal “take-once” service wrapper that:

consumes the route on first call (preserving the no-extra-clone optimization),

safely handles subsequent calls instead of panicking.

Note

There is already a TODO in the code about removing the unwraps. I’d like to implement this refactor along with a small test if that’s acceptable.

title: Check that number of path parameters matches tuple path extractor exactly
body:
- [x] I have looked for existing issues (including closed) about this

## Feature Request

Currently, `Path<String>` checks that there is exactly one path parameter, but `Path<(String, String)>` only checks that there is a **minimum** of two path parameters. It will then use the first two parameters as the actual values and discard the rest.

I think it would be much better to check that the number of path parameters matches the size of the tuple exactly to match the single parameter case.

### Motivation

<!--
Please describe the use case(s) or other motivation for the new feature.
-->
At work we had an incident that could have been prevented in multiple ways, one of which was if axum had caught the mismatch in parameter count. 

<details>
What happened is that a path segment was changed from a constant to a parameter like this:

`"/thing/:param1/:param2"` => `/:param0/:param1/:param2`

The handler (which was defined in a nested router) used `Path<(String, String)>` and was not updated. This meant that the new `:param0` was now used as `param1` and `:param1` as `param2`.

---
</details>

So for the sake of correctness of web servers I think it is good to be more strict in the case of tuple path extractors.
As for us, we will probably not use tuple path extractors anymore (not a big deal), at least until axum checks them more strictly as proposed here.

title: Consider making it easier to construct ErrorResponse from a non-IntoResponse error
body:
## Feature Request

### Motivation

People ask about short-circuiting from handler functions with non-`IntoResponse` errors somewhat frequently.

We already have `ErrorResponse` in `axum::response` for returning different error types from a handler function conveniently. However, right now it is quite annoying to construct one from a non-`IntoResponse` error type (see alternatives).

### Proposal

Add

```rust
impl ErrorResponse {
    fn internal_server_error(message: impl Display) -> Self {
        (StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, message.to_string()).into()
    }
}
```

to allow users to write

```rust
try_thing().map_err(ErrorResponse::internal_server_error)?;
```

### Alternatives

1. Expose a free function, same thing but less verbose

   ```rust
   try_thing().map_err(internal_server_error)?;
   ```
2. Do nothing. One can already do

   ```rust
   try_thing().map_err(|e| (StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, e.to_string()))?;
   ```

### Open questions

Should the `internal_server_error` function log the error as well?

title: impl FromRequest for BytesMut
body:
- [x] I have looked for existing issues (including closed) about this

## Feature Request

### Motivation

I'm working on a Fediverse server implementation, using axum as the web framework. Fediverse servers receive thousands of request every second, even for small instances, like the one I run, so performance is important. Because ActivityPub uses copious amounts of JSON, I figure it's best to use a high-performance JSON parser, like `simd-json`. However, `simd-json`'s `simd_json::from_slice` takes a mutable byte slice rather than an immutable one, so I can't use `Bytes` for that.

This is just one particular usecase, but I'm confident there are other performance-critical scenarios where you'd want a `BytesMut` value instead of a `Bytes` value.

### Proposal

In axum-core, add the impl, using the existing `Bytes` impl as a starting point.

### Alternatives

For my usecase, I could theoretically turn the `Bytes` value into a `Vec<u8>` and then into a `BytesMut`, but that would likely involve expensive copy operations that would nullify the performance gains from using `simd-json`.

title: Set tcp nodelay on sockets
body:
- [x] I have looked for existing issues (including closed) about this

## Feature Request

### Motivation
Currently `axum` does not set tcp-nodelay on accepted connections.
As demonstrated in this issue: https://github.com/hyperium/hyper/issues/3269 this default behaviour can heavily degrade performance in some use cases.

### Proposal
Add some way to set `TCP_NODELAY` on the accepted connections (via [`TcpStream::set_nodelay`](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/net/struct.TcpStream.html#method.set_nodelay)).

### Variants
1. Make it the default behaviour for `axum::serve` by just setting it on each accepted connection
2. Add a function to `axum::serve::Serve<>` (like `graceful_shutdown`) of which the usage could look something like this:
```rust
axum::serve(...).set_nodelay(true).await
```

### Some Notes/Questions
As far as I understood you want to keep this part of `axum` relatively simple and prefer to refer to `hyper-util` for more complex tasks. However, this would be a relatively small change (I can create a PR if you want) so it doesn't add much code complexity and can give huge performance boosts.

So I guess questions:
1. Do you want this at all?
2. If you do: What would you like for an interface?
